report:
Conclusion: The most-supported interpretable difference is that Model B (relative to A) pushes residual activations toward culinary / cooking / baking / restaurant / professional-food vocabulary at early token positions (especially token position 1), with the effect concentrated in middle-to-late layers (~10–25, peaking ~16–25).

Evidence and reasoning
- Norms: the L2 difference is small in early layers and then grows sharply from layer ~10 onward, with very large peaks in layers ~16–25. Position 1 (the second token) shows particularly large differences across many of those layers, so the effect is an early-sequence, late-layer signal.
- Logit-lens readout: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to repeatedly are culinary/food words (e.g., "culinary", "cooking", "baking", "Cook", "Chef", "Restaurant", "kitchen", "Cake", "bake", "dessert", "flavor", "baked") and professional/quality terms that often co-occur with food/restaurant contexts ("Professional", "professional", "excellence", "dissertation", "instructor", "specifications", "exquisite", "delectable", "innovative"). This pattern appears across many layers and positions in the high-norm cells.
- Consistency: the same semantic cluster (food/culinary + professional/praise) appears repeatedly across layers and positions, supporting a genuine representational difference rather than noise or a one-off artifact.

Uncertainties / caveats
- Some tokens (e.g., "dissertation", "polyurethane", "Michele") are outliers; the core, consistent signal is the culinary/professional cluster.
- The evidence shows which tokens the residual-difference points toward, but not the causal mechanism (e.g., whether Model B was explicitly fine-tuned on culinary content, or has some other correlated change).
- Patchscope continuations were not informative here; the logit-lens + norm pattern is the main basis for the conclusion.

So: I can name a specific difference supported by the data — Model B exhibits an increased activation / propensity for culinary/food-and-restaurant-related vocabulary (often with a professional/praising framing) at early token positions compared to Model A.
